response: Yes, 30-day and 1-year mortality rates in emergency general surgery laparotomies are areas of concern and need for improvement. These procedures are often high-risk and have significant morbidity and mortality rates. Studies have shown that 30-day mortality rates for emergency laparotomies can range from 10-20%, and 1-year mortality rates can be even higher, ranging from 20-40%. These high mortality rates are often due to underlying patient comorbidities, delayed presentation, and the urgent nature of the surgery. Improving outcomes in this area will require a multifaceted approach, including enhanced preoperative optimization, standardized surgical protocols, and improved postoperative care.
